topic.name: Harbor City heat pump incentives
topic.brief: Track residential heat pump rebates, tax credits, installer rules, and efficiency standards for homeowners and renters in Harbor City. I care about money available to households, eligibility changes, and application deadlines.

dimensions.name: Rebates
dimensions.description: Rebates and tax credits for households.

dimensions.name: Eligibility
dimensions.description: Who qualifies and how to apply.

dimensions.name: Efficiency standards
dimensions.description: Minimum efficiency rules for new units.

items.title: Harbor City expands heat pump rebates to renters
paragraphs: The Harbor City Energy Office said on Monday that renters can now claim heat pump rebates of up to $3,000 per household. The change takes effect for installations completed after January 15.
Landlords must sign a consent form before a renter can apply for the rebate. The office will publish the form on its website next week.
Officials said the change follows two years of complaints that renters were shut out of the program. About 41 percent of Harbor City households rent their homes.

items.title: State heat pump tax credit doubles for low income households
paragraphs: Low income households in the state can now claim a heat pump tax credit of $4,000, double the previous amount. The credit applies to heat pumps installed after the start of the next tax year.
Households earning less than 80 percent of the area median income qualify for the larger credit. Other households keep the existing $2,000 credit.
The state revenue department said claims will be filed with the normal income tax return. No separate application is needed.

items.title: State heat pump tax credit doubles for low income households
paragraphs: Low income households in the state can now claim a heat pump tax credit of $4,000, double the previous amount. The credit applies to heat pumps installed after the start of the next tax year.
Households earning less than 80 percent of the area median income qualify for the larger credit. Other households keep the existing $2,000 credit.
The state revenue department said claims will be filed with the normal income tax return. Distributed by Harbor Wire syndication.

items.title: New licensing rule for heat pump installers takes effect in March
paragraphs: Heat pump installers in Harbor City will need a state refrigerant license starting March 1. Contractors without the license cannot pull permits for new heat pump installations.
The rule is meant to cut refrigerant leaks from poorly installed systems. Inspectors found leaks in one of every eight systems checked last year.
Homeowners can check whether an installer is licensed on the state contractor board website before signing a contract.

items.title: Harbor City adopts a stricter heat pump efficiency standard
paragraphs: The city council voted 7 to 2 to require new heat pumps to meet the "cold climate" efficiency rating. The rule applies to units installed in new homes and major renovations.
Council members said the rating ensures units keep heating when outdoor temperatures drop below freezing. Older units lose much of their capacity in the city's coldest weeks.
Manufacturers have until the end of next year to supply compliant models to local distributors.

items.title: Heat pump rebate applications close on June 30
paragraphs: Harbor City homeowners have until June 30 to apply for this year's heat pump rebate. Applications received after the deadline will roll over into next year's program, which may offer smaller amounts.
The energy office urged applicants to upload invoices and proof of installation with the form. Incomplete applications were the most common reason for delays last year.
Rebate checks arrive about eight weeks after an application is approved.

items.title: Harbor City sets aside $12 million for heat pump rebates
paragraphs: The city budget for next year sets aside $12 million for residential heat pump rebates. That is enough to fund roughly 4,000 rebates at current amounts.
The money comes from a settlement with the regional gas utility over billing errors. Council members said the fund will be reviewed after one year.
Any money left at the end of the year returns to the general fund.

items.title: Contractors report a backlog of heat pump installations
paragraphs: Harbor City heat pump contractors say customers now wait an average of nine weeks for an installation. The backlog grew after the rebate program expanded last spring.
Several contractors are hiring apprentices to keep up with demand. Others have stopped taking new customers until the summer.
The energy office said it will track wait times in its quarterly report.

items.title: Harbor Power tests smart thermostats with heat pump owners
paragraphs: Harbor Power is recruiting 500 heat pump owners for a smart thermostat pilot this winter. Participants get a free thermostat and a small credit on their bill.
The utility wants to learn whether heat pumps can shift heating to cheaper hours. Results are expected next fall.
The pilot is not connected to the city rebate program.

items.title: Geothermal heat pumps draw interest from Harbor City schools
paragraphs: The Harbor City school district is studying geothermal heat pumps for three elementary schools. A consultant will report on costs and drilling conditions in the spring.
District officials said geothermal systems could cut heating bills at the schools by a third. The project would need voter approval for a bond.
The study does not cover private homes.

items.title: A heat pump buyers guide for Harbor City winters
paragraphs: Choosing a heat pump for Harbor City winters starts with the right size for the home. An installer should calculate the heating load room by room.
Cold climate models cost more but keep working in deep cold. Ask for the unit's capacity at five degrees Fahrenheit.

items.title: Harbor City Heat win third straight home game
paragraphs: The Harbor City Heat beat the Valley Rovers 102 to 95 on Saturday night for their third straight home win. Guard Mia Torres scored 31 points.
The Heat play their next three games on the road. Tickets for the next home game go on sale on Tuesday.
Coach Ray Linden said the team's defense has improved since the start of the season.

items.title: Pumpkin festival returns to the Harbor City waterfront
paragraphs: The annual pumpkin festival returns to the waterfront this weekend with carving contests and a farmers market. Organizers expect about 20,000 visitors.
Parking will be limited near the pier, and extra buses will run from downtown. The festival runs from ten in the morning to six in the evening.
Proceeds support the city's food bank.

items.title: Rooftop solar permits reach a record in Harbor County
paragraphs: Harbor County issued 1,900 rooftop solar permits in the last quarter, a record for the county. Most were for single family homes.
Installers credit falling panel prices and faster permit reviews. The county now approves most solar permits within five days.
Battery storage permits also rose sharply.

items.title: One weird trick to triple your heat pump rebate
paragraphs: Homeowners are tripling their heat pump rebates with one simple trick that officials do not want you to know. Click now to learn more.
Limited time offer. Act today before the secret is gone.

items.title: Harbor City raises renter heat pump rebates to $4,500
paragraphs: Renters in Harbor City can now claim heat pump rebates of up to $4,500 per household, up from $3,000. The higher cap applies to applications filed after March 1.
Landlords must still sign the consent form before a renter can apply for the rebate. The energy office said demand from renters was higher than expected.
About 41 percent of Harbor City households rent their homes.

items.title: Harbor City expands heat pump rebates to renters
paragraphs: The Harbor City Energy Office says renters can now claim heat pump rebates of up to $3,000 per household. The change takes effect for installations completed after January 15.
Landlords must sign a consent form before a renter can apply for the rebate. The office will publish the form on its website.
The change follows two years of complaints that renters were shut out of the program, officials said.

items.title: State heat pump tax credit doubles for low income households
paragraphs: Low income households in the state can now claim a heat pump tax credit of $4,000, double the previous amount. The credit applies to heat pumps installed after the start of the next tax year.
Households earning less than 80 percent of the area median income qualify for the larger credit. Other households keep the existing $2,000 credit.
The state revenue department said claims will be filed with the normal income tax return. No separate application is needed.

items.title: Harbor City delays its heat pump efficiency standard to 2028
paragraphs: The city council voted to delay the cold climate efficiency rating for new heat pumps until January 2028. Distributors said they could not stock enough compliant models by the original date.
The rule will still apply to units installed in new homes and major renovations once it takes effect.
Council members said they will not delay the standard again.

items.title: Community college launches heat pump installer training
paragraphs: Harbor Community College will offer a twelve week heat pump installer course starting in May. The course prepares students for the state refrigerant license.
Tuition is free for Harbor City residents through a grant from the energy office. Graduates will be placed with local contractors.
The college expects to train 60 installers in the first year.

items.title: Landlord groups sue over the renter heat pump consent rule
paragraphs: Two landlord associations sued Harbor City over the consent form renters need before claiming a heat pump rebate. The groups say the form makes landlords liable for installation damage.
A judge will hear the case next month. The energy office said rebates will keep flowing while the case is pending.
Renter advocates called the lawsuit an attempt to slow the program.

items.title: How low income households can claim the doubled heat pump tax credit
paragraphs: Households claiming the doubled heat pump tax credit should keep the installer invoice and the product certificate. Both are needed if the revenue department asks for proof.
Tax preparers in Harbor City say most households will claim the credit on form 5695. Free filing help is available at city libraries in February and March.
The credit cannot be combined with a rebate for the same unit in the same year.

items.title: School district plans a geothermal heat pump loop
paragraphs: The Harbor City school district will drill a shared geothermal heat pump loop for three elementary schools if voters approve the bond. Drilling would start in the summer.
The district consultant estimated the loop would cut heating bills at the schools by a third. The bond vote is in November.
The project does not cover private homes.

items.title: Heat wave strains the Harbor City power grid
paragraphs: Harbor Power asked customers to cut electricity use on Tuesday as a heat wave pushed demand to a record. Temperatures reached 101 degrees downtown.
The utility said air conditioners were running at full power across the city. No outages were reported.
Cooling centers will stay open through the weekend.

items.title: Harbor City Heat hockey opener sells out
paragraphs: Tickets for the Harbor City Heat hockey season opener sold out in under an hour. The team plays the Northport Gulls on October 12.
The arena added 400 standing room tickets for students. The season runs through March.
The Heat finished second in the league last season.

topic.name: Harbor City electric ferries and buses
topic.brief: Follow Harbor City's plans to electrify its ferry fleet and bus routes: vessel and bus purchases, charging infrastructure, budgets, schedules, and service changes riders will notice.

dimensions.name: Ferries
dimensions.description: Electric ferry purchases, deliveries, and service.

items.title: Harbor City orders two battery electric ferries
paragraphs: Harbor City Transit ordered two battery electric ferries from Northshore Marine for $38 million. Each vessel will carry 300 passengers between downtown and Gull Island.
The ferries will replace two diesel boats built in the 1980s. Transit officials expect the switch to cut ferry fuel costs by about 70 percent.
Delivery of the first vessel is planned for late 2027.

items.title: Harbor City orders two battery electric ferries
paragraphs: Harbor City Transit ordered two battery electric ferries from Northshore Marine for $38 million. Each vessel will carry 300 passengers between downtown and Gull Island.
The ferries will replace two diesel boats built in the 1980s. Transit officials expect the switch to cut ferry fuel costs by about 70 percent.
Delivery of the first vessel is planned for late 2027. Distributed by Harbor Wire syndication.

items.title: Ferry charging dock construction starts at Pier 9
paragraphs: Crews began building the ferry charging dock at Pier 9 on Wednesday, the first step toward the city's "zero emission" ferry route. The dock will charge a ferry in about 15 minutes.
Harbor Power is adding a substation near the pier to supply the chargers. The work will close part of the pier walkway until spring.
The dock is funded by a federal port grant.

items.title: Electric buses will run on routes 4 and 11 from April
paragraphs: Harbor City Transit will move routes 4 and 11 to electric buses starting April 6. The two routes carry about 9,000 riders a day.
Schedules will not change, but some stops will move to make room for charging at the route ends. Riders can see the new stop locations on the transit website.
More routes will switch as buses arrive.

items.title: Council approves $48 million for transit electrification
paragraphs: The Harbor City council approved $48 million for ferry and bus electrification over the next four years. The money covers vessels, buses, and chargers.
About half the total comes from federal grants. The rest comes from the city's transit bond.
The council will review spending every six months.

items.title: Bus fares will rise by 25 cents in July
paragraphs: Harbor City bus fares will rise by 25 cents on July 1, the first increase in six years. A single ride will cost $2.75.
Monthly passes will rise by $5. Reduced fares for seniors and students will not change.
Transit officials said rising labor costs drove the increase.

items.title: A short history of Harbor City's wooden ferries
paragraphs: Harbor City's first ferries were wooden steamers that crossed to Gull Island in the 1890s. The last wooden ferry retired in 1951.
The maritime museum keeps the steamer Gull Queen on display at Pier 2. Volunteers lead tours on weekends.
The museum plans an exhibit on the new electric ferries next year.

items.title: Harbor City marathon closes downtown streets on Sunday
paragraphs: The Harbor City marathon will close downtown streets from six in the morning until two in the afternoon on Sunday. About 8,000 runners are registered.
Several bus routes will detour around the course. Ferry service will run on its normal schedule.
Race organizers recommend arriving early.

items.title: Scooter share expands to three new neighborhoods
paragraphs: The scooter share program will expand to Eastgate, Millbrook, and the Old Port next month. The operator is adding 600 scooters.
Riders pay a dollar to unlock a scooter and 30 cents a minute. Parking corrals will be painted near major intersections.
The city will review the program after one year.

items.title: Free ferry passes for everyone, claim yours now
paragraphs: Everyone in Harbor City can claim free ferry passes this week only. Enter your card number to receive yours.
Offer ends soon.

items.title: First electric ferry delivery moves up to September 2027
paragraphs: Northshore Marine will deliver Harbor City's first battery electric ferry in September 2027, three months earlier than planned. The second vessel follows in early 2028.
The ferries will carry 300 passengers each between downtown and Gull Island. Crews will train on the first vessel before it enters service.
Transit officials said the earlier date will cut diesel use sooner.

items.title: Harbor City orders two battery electric ferries
paragraphs: Harbor City Transit has ordered two battery electric ferries from Northshore Marine for $38 million. Each vessel will carry 300 passengers between downtown and Gull Island.
The ferries replace two diesel boats built in the 1980s. Officials expect the switch to cut ferry fuel costs by about 70 percent.
The first vessel is planned for late 2027.

items.title: Bus depot gets 30 new chargers for electric buses
paragraphs: Harbor City Transit installed 30 chargers at the Westside bus depot to serve the electric buses on routes 4 and 11. The chargers can refill a bus overnight.
The depot will add 20 more chargers next year as more electric buses arrive.
The project was finished two weeks ahead of schedule.

items.title: Weekly fare cap proposed for frequent bus and ferry riders
paragraphs: Harbor City Transit proposed a weekly fare cap so riders never pay more than $25 in a week. Riders would need a reloadable card to qualify.
The transit board will vote on the proposal next month. A public hearing is set for the 18th.
The cap would cover both buses and ferries.

items.title: Ferry crews begin battery safety training
paragraphs: Harbor City ferry crews began battery safety training this week ahead of the first electric ferry delivery. The course covers fire response and charging procedures.
Every captain and deckhand must finish the course before working on the new vessels.
The training is run by the state maritime academy.

items.title: Summer concert series announces its lineup
paragraphs: The Harbor City summer concert series will feature twelve bands at the waterfront park. Concerts start at seven in the evening every Friday.
Admission is free, and food trucks will line the park entrance.
The series is in its twentieth year.

feedback.reason: Route changes are what I need to plan around.

topic.name: Quantum error correction hardware
topic.brief: Track superconducting and trapped ion quantum computing hardware progress on error correction: logical qubits, physical error rates, code distances, and decoder speed.

items.title: Quantum Cafe opens on Main Street with a computing theme
paragraphs: The Quantum Cafe opened on Main Street this week with a menu named after famous computer scientists. The owner, a retired engineer, decorated the walls with old circuit boards.
The cafe serves coffee, sandwiches, and a dessert called the error correction cake. It opens at seven every morning.
The owner plans a monthly trivia night about science and technology.

items.title: Harbor City libraries extend weekend hours
paragraphs: All Harbor City library branches will stay open until eight in the evening on Saturdays starting next month. The change follows a survey of 3,000 library users.
The central library will also open on Sunday mornings. Staffing costs are covered by a state grant.
Story time for children moves to Saturday afternoons.

items.title: Road repairs will close two lanes on Harbor Avenue
paragraphs: Crews will close two lanes of Harbor Avenue for six weeks starting Monday to repair the road surface. Traffic will be reduced to one lane in each direction.
The city recommends using Pier Street as a detour. Buses will keep their normal stops.
The repairs cost $2.1 million.

items.title: Students build robots for the Harbor City science fair
paragraphs: More than 200 students entered the Harbor City science fair this year, many with robots and coding projects. The winner built a robot that sorts recycling.
Judges included engineers from local companies and the community college. Prizes include summer internships.
The fair will be held again next spring.

items.title: Ferry schedule changes for the winter season
paragraphs: The Gull Island ferry will run every 45 minutes instead of every 30 minutes from November through March. The last ferry leaves downtown at eleven in the evening.
Holiday service will follow the Sunday schedule. Riders can check departures on the transit website.
The summer schedule returns in April.
